title: Pisces Emoji ♓ Meaning: Two Fish and a Dreamy Reputation
description: The ♓ Pisces emoji represents the Fish, the last zodiac sign, for February 19 to March 20 birthdays. See how it signals dreaminess and deep feelings.
summary: The ♓ Pisces emoji is the symbol of Pisces, the Fish, the twelfth and final zodiac sign, for people born from about February 19 to March 20. It names a sign and evokes its reputation for being dreamy, empathetic, artistic, and easily lost in feelings.
meaning: The Pisces glyph is two curved lines facing away from each other, tied together by a bar through the middle. It pictures a pair of fish swimming in opposite directions while bound by a cord, the image attached to the constellation since antiquity. The emoji closes out the zodiac set and is used for birthdays in late February and March, just before the cycle restarts with Aries.

Astrology calls Pisces mutable water. Its rulers are Jupiter in the older scheme and Neptune in the modern one, and Neptune's associations with dreams, illusion, and the sea shape the sign's image. A Pisces is said to absorb other people's moods, live half in imagination, and feel everything deeply. As the last sign, it is sometimes described as carrying a little of all the others.

The online caricature is tender and spacey: crying to a song, zoning out mid-conversation, falling in love with a stranger on the train, forgetting where the car is parked. Pisceans use ♓ to confess those moments, and friends use it for the most sensitive member of the group. The opposite-facing fish also get quoted when someone feels pulled two ways or wants to escape reality for a while.

contexts.label: In bios and birthday posts
contexts.body: ♓ accompanies dates from late February to mid March and often sits beside 🐟, 🌊, or 🔮. Musicians, painters, and poets born under the sign like to mention it, since Pisces is promoted as the artist of the zodiac. It also appears in chart listings as a moon or rising sign.

contexts.label: In texting
contexts.body: It explains sudden tears, daydreaming, and intuitive hunches: "I just knew, ♓." Friends use it tenderly, since the stereotype is gentle. It can excuse flakiness as well, as when someone forgets a plan because they were lost in thought. Fellow water signs often reply with their own emoji in sympathy.

contexts.label: From a crush
contexts.body: If a date shares that they are a ♓, astrology fans expect a romantic who idealizes partners and needs reassurance. The emoji is an invitation to compare signs. Do not read more into it than that; plenty of people mention their sign out of habit.

confusedWith.difference: 🐟 is an ordinary fish, used for fishing, aquariums, seafood, and occasionally as a Christian symbol. Pisceans add it for decoration. ♓ is the astrological glyph and would not be used to talk about actual fish.

♊ also shows a doubled figure joined together, which leads to mix-ups at small sizes. Gemini's two lines are straight and upright with bars at the top and bottom. Pisces has two outward-bowing curves joined by one bar across the middle.

avoid: Do not use ♓ to dismiss someone's emotions as "just a Pisces thing" when they are truly upset.
Avoid it for seafood or fishing posts, where the animal emoji is clearer.
design: Two white arcs curving away from each other like back-to-back parentheses, connected by a horizontal line, on a purple square. Some people see a letter H with bowed sides. Platforms agree on the shape, and the emoji is the final tile in the zodiac row on most keyboards.

faqs.a: Approximately February 19 to March 20. Pisces follows Aquarius and ends at the March equinox, when Aries starts a new cycle. Cusp dates can differ by a day between years.

faqs.q: Why does the Pisces symbol look like an H?
faqs.a: The two curved sides are fish and the crossbar is the cord that ties them. It only resembles an H by coincidence. The fish face opposite ways, often read as a pull between fantasy and reality.

faqs.q: What does ♓ mean in a text?
faqs.a: That the sender or the person being discussed is a Pisces, or is acting like the stereotype: emotional, dreamy, intuitive. It is used warmly far more often than critically.

faqs.q: Is Pisces the last zodiac sign?
faqs.a: Yes. It is the twelfth sign in the standard order, which starts with Aries at the March equinox. That placement is why astrologers associate Pisces with endings, release, and wisdom gathered from the whole cycle.
